summary.title: Docker Security Cheat Sheet
summary.one_liner: You learn a checklist of Docker container security rules, from not exposing the Docker socket and running as a non-root user to limiting capabilities, setting read-only filesystems, and using rootless mode.
takeaways: Never expose the Docker daemon socket or TCP API, and do not mount /var/run/docker.sock into containers, since socket access equals root on the host.
Run containers as an unprivileged user, drop all Linux capabilities and add only the ones needed, and avoid --privileged.
Use --security-opt=no-new-privileges, keep the root filesystem read-only with --read-only and --tmpfs, and set resource limits.
Publishing ports with -p can bypass UFW; bind published ports to 127.0.0.1 or use ufw-docker to enforce firewall rules.
Keep the host kernel and Docker Engine updated, scan images in CI/CD, and consider rootless mode or Podman for stronger isolation.
summary.summary: This OWASP cheat sheet gives a numbered list of rules (Rule #0 to #13) for securing Docker containers, each with short explanations and command or Kubernetes examples. It covers the daemon socket, user and capability settings, privilege escalation, networking and UFW port-publishing pitfalls, seccomp/AppArmor/SELinux profiles, resource limits, read-only filesystems, CI/CD scanning, logging level, rootless mode, secrets, and supply chain practices. It ends with a brief section on Podman as a daemonless, rootless alternative.
